name: team-work
description: Collaborative work planning for teams using Claude Code. Nineteen skills. Shift-left gates (requirements → agreement → handoff; all wiki-required, all writing their artifact back into the wiki): /work-analyze (deeply analyze a requirements document against the ACTUAL codebase — auto-resolved from sibling repos under a shared parent — and the wiki's prior decisions, giving every requirement an explicit verdict: BUILD AS WRITTEN / BUILD WITH CHANGES / RECOMMEND AGAINST / DEFER / NEEDS DECISION, each backed by file:line evidence or a cited decision, with an alternative for anything recommended against; routes open questions to named owners by audience and surfaces risks, implicit scope, and what the release will not deliver), /work-signoff (turn the review meeting's transcript into the concise agreed statement of what the release delivers — the thing stakeholders sign instead of reconciling a drifted requirements doc; reconciles decisions against the prior analysis, supersedes any earlier sign-off while keeping it as a citable baseline with a 'what changed since' section, and splits still-open items into blocking vs non-blocking so the build can start honestly), /work-handoff (generate a developer onboarding guide from the work plan, its tracker issues, and the wiki — the dependency map is READ from the tracker's real link graph, never inferred; maps each item to its repo and stack, mines the authoritative design and its decisions into a document index with reading order, and leads getting-unblocked with querying the wiki rather than interrupting the lead). Knowledge layer (LLM-maintained SDLC wiki — an Open Knowledge Format (OKF v0.1) bundle: typed markdown concept pages with YAML frontmatter, per-directory index.md navigation, okf_version at the bundle root, cross-linked into a graph): /work-wiki (init/repair a configurable wiki root with qmd search; README.md catalog + OKF index.md nav + standard relative markdown links that render on GitHub and Obsidian; offers GitHub Pages hosting on finish), /work-ingest (classify a client call/doc, archive it verbatim+categorized under sources/ as an audit trail — converting PDF/xlsx/docx to markdown while preserving the original — then integrate into requirement/entity/concept/decision/incident pages where every claim cites its source via a relative markdown link), /work-ask (qmd hybrid search → cited answer → file it back so explorations compound), /work-lint (health-check: contradictions, stale claims, orphans, missing pages/cross-refs, broken/dangling links, legacy [[wikilinks]]/index.md, source gaps), /work-upgrade (migrate an older wiki to current conventions: index.md → README.md via git mv, rewrite [[wikilinks]] → relative markdown links, verify link integrity, plus an OKF v0.1 conformance pass — backfill required `type` frontmatter, generate per-directory index.md nav, add bundle-root okf_version; idempotent), /work-publish (host the wiki as a MkDocs Material site on SS&C GitHub Enterprise Pages — pages.code.ssnc.dev/<org>/<repo>/ — styled with the SS&C Blue Stone look by default: SS&C Blue #0077C8 + Teal accent, full brand palette, Calibri typography, bordered tables, light/dark, from a canonical extra.css embedded in the skill so the brand applies even when the template repo is unreachable, logos fetched best-effort, opt-out to plain Material; scaffolds mkdocs.yml with docs_dir at the wiki root and auto-generated nav, requirements.txt, and a self-hosted GitHub Actions workflow that deploys via gh-deploy to gh-pages; auto-enables Pages via the API once gh-pages exists and verifies the live site; warns that excluding sources/ breaks every citation link and recommends restricting viewers instead; code.ssnc.dev only, idempotent), /wiki-source (turn a code repository into wiki knowledge in three steps: generate/refresh C4 architecture docs in docs/c4/ by delegating to /agent-orch:c4; walk the source to write a business-domain guide at docs/wiki/domain/ and a technical/DevSecOps reference at docs/wiki/technical/, cross-linked to existing repo docs; then /work-ingest the repo's markdown into the wiki — honors ingest_mode, commits in place), /wiki-source-branch (the same pipeline over the ENTIRE repo, always committed on the current branch with no scope prompt/worktree/PR; no-ops cleanly without a wiki; called automatically by /agent-orch:make after it commits code so the wiki stays in sync with every feature). Planning→release: /work-prep (SDLC intake), /work-plan (plan to Jira), /work-pop (pick next item), /work-report (HTML report with top-of-page Jira status breakdown — Open/In Progress/In Review/Done/Blocked/Total/%Done — plus Recently Shipped panel), /work-recap (time-windowed Markdown + Bluestone PPTX recap of Jira activity, commits, and agent-orch sessions — every Jira entry is self-contained with description, last comment + count, attachments, and full metadata so stakeholders can read without clicking into Jira), /groom (worktree-based backlog grooming with Jira lifecycle, transitions tracking issue to Done, and produces a self-contained Markdown + Bluestone PDF report with description, last comment, comment count, attachments, and metadata for every groomed issue), /create-release (tags, release notes, PDFs, GitHub releases), /plugin-feedback (structured feedback wizard → Jira ticket in AITOOLS). Opt-in extensibility framework (config files under .claude/ssnc-team-work/ with before/replace/after agent hooks, skill hook points; zero behaviour change by default). Full SDLC from client call to requirements to /make to release.
